title: Integers within plus or minus (2^53 - 1), refused beyond (FORMA-182, design 3 lines 86-92, design 4 rule 3, DR-9)
contract: A Rust integer bound for a page (i8 to i64, u8 to u64, isize, usize) is compared in the integer domain before any conversion: inside -(2^53 - 1)..=(2^53 - 1) it is encoded exactly and written as its decimal digits; beyond, the render refuses it with RENDER-401 instead of letting it arrive rounded. A finite float keeps its own admission (RENDER-402, finite only): an integer-valued float past 2^53 is admitted and formatted by rule 2, because its origin carries no exactness claim. The client reads the envelope with JSON.parse, so an admitted integer is a safe integer there and String() spells the same digits.
consumers: crates/forma-ir/tests/page_props.rs > integer_vectors_are_admitted_or_refused_in_the_integer_domain (encode_props on i64 and u64 origins, f64 origins)
crates/forma-ir/src/walker.rs > value_rule_vectors (an admitted integer as DYN_TEXT)
packages/core/src/dom/__tests__/value-rules.test.ts (Number.isSafeInteger and BigInt as the oracle; JSON.parse round trip; h() text)
note: Hand-enumerated. `kind` names the Rust origin type the vector is encoded from; `lexeme` is the exact decimal, never a JSON number, so no reader rounds it before the check.
